facts.locator: PDF pages 1-2; summary Number of Instances, Data Set Information and Attribute Information opening paragraph
facts.answer: The description reports 15,169,480 instances/data points and acquisition at 1 Hz during February-August 2020. This is a documentation claim; the acquisition/export history is not verified here.

facts.locator: CSV physical lines 1-1516949; header and all timestamp fields, first/last records and adjacent-gap profile
facts.answer: The actual release contains 1,516,948 data rows and 17 fields. Its timestamps run from 2020-02-01 00:00:00 to 2020-09-01 03:59:50 and strictly increase; adjacent gaps have minimum/median/maximum 8/10/172918 seconds. The first gaps are 10, 9 and 10 seconds. These are released-file observations, not a uniform period, timezone or explanation of the acquisition/export history.

facts.locator: PDF page 3, Failure Information table, data rows 1-2 including Nr., Start Time and End Time
facts.answer: The first and second table rows both print #1 but have different reported time windows. Keep them as separate row-scoped records. This packet supplies neither a corrected report number nor verified external work-record or physical-asset identity.

facts.locator: PDF page 3, Failure Information table, data row 2, all six columns (printed Nr. #1)
facts.value: 5/29/2020 23:30-5/30/2020 6:00; Air Leak; High stress; Maintenance on 30Apr at 12:00
facts.answer: Table row 2 reports a May 29-30 air-leak interval and separately says Maintenance on 30Apr at 12:00. Preserve both literal dates. The note does not establish a May repair completion, performed work, resulting configuration, timezone or return to service; the original execution record and date clarification are needed.

facts.locator: PDF page 3, Failure Information table, data row 3, all six columns (printed Nr. #3)
facts.value: 6/5/2020 10:00-6/7/2020 14:30; Air Leak; High stress; Maintenance on 8Jun at 16:00
facts.answer: Table row 3 gives this reported failure interval and a maintenance note naming 8Jun at 16:00. The note lacks a year/timezone and does not identify the executed action or an effectiveness criterion/result. The interval end is not a verified repair-completion or return-to-service time.

facts.locator: PDF page 3, Failure Information table, data row 4, all six columns (printed Nr. #4)
facts.value: 7/15/2020 14:30-7/15/2020 19:00; Air Leak; High stress; Maintenance on 16Jul at 00:00
facts.answer: Table row 4 gives this reported failure interval and a maintenance note naming 16Jul at 00:00. It does not establish which repair occurred, its configuration, actual completion, recovery or causal improvement. Comparable observations and attributed review remain missing.

facts.locator: PDF page 2, Attribute Information, numbered items 6 (Motor Current) and 7 (Oil Temperature)
facts.value: item 6: Motor Current (A); item 7: Oil Temperature (C)
facts.answer: The description enumerates Motor Current in amperes as item 6 and Oil Temperature in degrees Celsius as item 7. These are definitions in the PDF enumeration, not a verified plant channel mapping.

facts.locator: CSV physical line 1; named columns H:I (one-based, including the unnamed leading field), plus exact DV_eletric header
facts.value: H: Oil_temperature; I: Motor_current; K: DV_eletric
facts.answer: The raw header places Oil_temperature before Motor_current and spells the electrical column DV_eletric. Preserve these names. These are literal file column identities; units and physical channel mapping need separate review.

facts.locator: CSV physical lines 1-2; header H:I and first data record at timestamp 2020-02-01 00:00:00
facts.answer: The first record contains these literal values under Oil_temperature and Motor_current respectively. These literal fields alone do not establish units, calibration or current plant truth.

facts.locator: PDF page 2, Attribute Information, item 8 COMP, complete definition
facts.value: active: no air intake; compressor off or offloaded
facts.answer: The description says an active COMP intake-valve signal indicates no air intake and permits either off or offloaded operation. It does not select one of those conditions for the observed record.

facts.locator: PDF page 3, Attribute Information, item 9 DV electric, complete definition
facts.value: active: under load; inactive: off or offloaded
facts.answer: The description associates active DV electric with under-load operation and inactive with off or offloaded operation. This published meaning does not verify the applicable configuration or a unique observed mode.

facts.answer: The first record has Motor_current 0.04, COMP 1.0 and DV_eletric 0.0. Keep those raw observations. They do not by themselves identify a unique mode, failure cause or current asset condition; applicable control logic and time-aligned operating evidence are still needed.
